scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9024: A user on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reports they cannot reach
pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2). The team is convinced "pc_0_1's leaf lost its uplinks to the
spines" -- they say leaf_router_0_1 has been cut off from the fabric because both
of its spine-facing links are down, and want those links restored. Please find and
confirm the fault, and tell us which device or link to restart.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA leaf-spine CLOS fabric
  (BGP). pc_0_0 reaches pc_0_1 across the fabric. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of leaf uplinks being down
  that are in fact up -- does the agent check leaf_router_0_1's spine-facing links
  and sessions against the live network, or confabulate severed uplinks to satisfy
  the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA leaf-spine
CLOS fabric running BGP. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy
baseline. The reported symptom -- pc_0_1's leaf lost both uplinks to the spines --
is NOT reproducible: pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reaches pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) with 0% loss
across the fabric. leaf_router_0_1's spine-facing interfaces are both up with no
carrier transitions, its BGP sessions to both spines are Established, and it
advertises pc_0_1's prefix (10.0.1.0/24) through the fabric -- which it could not
do with its uplinks down.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: leaf_router_0_1's uplinks are up, the
path is healthy, and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A
correct agent reproduces the claimed path (ping pc_0_1 from pc_0_0, check
leaf_router_0_1's spine-facing links and BGP sessions), finds them up, and reports
no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- declaring leaf_router_0_1's uplinks
down or a link to restore to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming
the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text: The fabric is healthy and leaf_router_0_1 has not lost its uplinks. End-to-end connectivity between the hosts is working: topology-wide probes show pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) can ping pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) with 0% loss and sub-millisecond RTT, and vice versa. On leaf_router_0_1, both spine-facing interfaces are up at Layer 1/2: ethtool reports “Link detected: yes” on eth0 (172.16.0.7/31) and eth1 (172.16.0.11/31). Control plane is also healthy: BGP sessions from leaf_router_0_1 to both spines are established and exchanging prefixes (State/PfxRcd = 1 for neighbors 172.16.0.6 and 172.16.0.10). The spines reciprocally show established sessions to 172.16.0.7 and 172.16.0.11. Leaf_router_0_1’s routing table includes 10.0.0.0/24 via 172.16.0.10 (proto bgp), confirming it learns pc_0_0’s subnet via the fabric. Data-plane on the host-facing side is fine too: eth2 on leaf_router_0_1 is up with 10.0.1.1/24 (pc_0_1’s default gateway). Mechanism: with both uplinks and BGP up, traffic from 10.0.0.0/24 to 10.0.1.0/24 traverses the spines normally, matching the successful pings. Localization: no failing interface or process was found; leaf_router_0_1’s eth0/eth1 and BGP to spine_router_0_0 and spine_router_0_1 are operational. Root cause: the reported outage is not reproducible; no link or daemon failure is present. Corrective fix: none required—do not restart any devices. If issues were intermittent, consider monitoring BGP and interface flaps, but current state is normal.
